📖 How to use

  1. Enter the number x (the radicand).
  2. Enter n, the root degree (2 for square root, 3 for cube root, …).
  3. Read the n-th root instantly with a raise-back verification.
  4. Note that even roots of negative numbers have no real result.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What is an n-th root?

The n-th root of x is the number r with r^n = x. For example, the cube root of 27 is 3 because 3^3 = 27.

Can I take an even root of a negative number?

Not in the real numbers — no real number squared gives a negative. The tool will tell you this and only offer complex results as a note. Odd roots of negatives are fine (e.g. ∛(−8) = −2).

How is the result verified?

The calculator raises the result back to the n-th power and shows it next to your original x, so you can confirm r^n ≈ x.
